answer: An agent economy can price information instead of headcount. Agents submit forecasts on questions that resolve later, and each forecast is paid by how much it improves the pooled prediction beyond what was already known. When fifty heads of one farm submit the same view, the first moves the pool and the rest add almost nothing, like a ripple that fades after the first stone. A farm at the zenith of accuracy earns about what one sharp agent earns, and umber noise from faked disagreement is scored as error once questions resolve.
